metaTitle: Skid vs. Pallet: Differences, Uses, and Plastic vs. Wood — AGL Pallet
metaDescription: The difference between a skid and a pallet, when each makes sense, a side-by-side comparison table, and how plastic pallets compare with wood.

sections.heading: The difference in one line
paragraphs: A skid is a single-deck platform on runners, with no bottom deck. A pallet adds a bottom deck, or uses blocks between two decks. In practice, many shippers and carriers say "skid" for any pallet, so when it matters, describe the construction instead of relying on the word.
Skids came first. They were dragged or lifted with early platform trucks; the bottom deck arrived with the forklift, when loads began to be stacked and racked.

table.caption: Skid vs. pallet at a glance

table.note: Typical characteristics. A heavy-duty engineered skid and a light one-way pallet can reverse several of these.

sections.heading: When a skid makes sense
list: Heavy machinery or castings that ship once and get bolted down.
Loads lifted by crane or moved on rollers, where runners are an advantage.
Products that will not be stacked or racked.
Cost-sensitive one-way shipments where a bottom deck adds nothing.
after: For loads that outweigh a standard pallet several times over, runner size, spacing, and fasteners should be engineered to the load. See [custom and engineered pallets](/custom-engineered/).

sections.heading: Plastic vs. wood pallets
paragraphs: The skid-or-pallet question often comes with a material question. Wood is the default for most North American shipping; plastic has a place in closed loops and sanitary environments.

table.caption: Plastic vs. wood pallets
rows: Boards and stringers can be replaced
Easy; mills cut to any footprint
Tied to molds; custom sizes are costly
Washable; common in food and pharma
Wood is widely reused and repurposed
Resin can be reground where programs exist
table.note: APHIS lists plastic pallets among materials not subject to its wood packaging regulations. See [heat-treated pallets and ISPM-15](/resources/heat-treated-pallets-ispm-15/).

after: AGL's line is wood: stock and custom pallets, engineered skids, and crates, sourced through qualified mills. See [products](/products/).

items.question: Is a skid the same as a pallet?
answer: Not strictly. A skid has runners and a top deck but no bottom deck; a pallet adds a bottom deck or uses blocks between two decks. In everyday shipping the words are used interchangeably, so describe the construction on the order if it matters.

items.question: Should heavy machinery ship on a skid or a pallet?
answer: Heavy machinery often ships on a skid, because runners can be sized to the load and suit crane lifts and rollers. If the unit will be stacked, racked, or moved by pallet jack, a pallet or an engineered design is a better fit.
